profile.campus: Chicago metro, Illinois (Equinix Chicago campus, CH1-CH5 and CH7)
profile.address: 1905 Lunt Avenue, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007
profile.reading:
Equinix CH3 stands at 1905 Lunt Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, a Chicago area suburb adjacent to O'Hare International Airport that a Daily Herald profile of the village described as home to North America's largest industrial park, with more than 3,600 businesses located within it. Equinix purchased the underlying office and warehouse complex in June 2006 for 9.75 million dollars from Amalgamated Bank of Chicago, according to Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of the building's opening, then invested to convert it into a data center. The first phase opened October 24, 2007, representing a 175 million dollar investment delivering 228,000 square feet of space designed for approximately 2,500 cabinets, with a planned second phase to add capacity for roughly 1,300 more cabinets, and Data Center Dynamics described it at the time as the largest of Equinix's then 35 global data centers, absorbing over 300 existing customers who had previously used two smaller, already established Equinix locations in the Chicago area favored by low latency financial trading firms.

A separate account from design build contractor ClayCorp's own project page describes CH3 as a three level, 240,000 square foot, 29 million dollar core and shell Tier IV building with N+1 or greater uninterruptible power supply redundancy and backup generator systems, designed by architecture firm Sheehan Partners and honored with an AIA Chicago 2008 Design Award for Distinguished Building. That figure differs somewhat from the Data Center Dynamics account of the 2006 to 2007 build, likely reflecting a different measurement basis or project phase, and the two are not reconciled here. A later expansion of the building, described on the own project page of a separate contractor, FCL Builders, put CH3 at 379,662 square feet total, including 133,987 square feet of raised floor colocation space, rated for 10.8 megawatts of power at N+1 redundancy and N+2 cooling redundancy, a still larger figure consistent with continued build out of the site well beyond its original 2006 to 2007 construction.

Equinix's own current site for this building states a narrower, more recent figure of 196,151 square feet of disclosed colocation space, with N+1 uninterruptible power supply redundancy, two generators providing more than 30 hours of autonomy at full load, and N+20 percent cooling redundancy, but publishes no current megawatt power capacity figure for the building. None of these four square footage figures, 196,151, 228,000, 240,000, and 379,662, are treated here as interchangeable, since they likely describe different measurement bases, disclosed colocation space versus total building shell, at different points across nearly two decades of construction and expansion.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, converted to a real estate investment trust structure in 2015, and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across more than 70 metro markets worldwide, with Chicago positioned by the company as the fourth largest primary data center market in the United States and a hub for its financial services interconnection business, connecting trading firms, exchanges, and cloud providers through Equinix Fabric and cross connects. ComEd, the regional electric utility, completed a new five acre substation in Elk Grove in November 2021 specifically to expand transmission and distribution capacity supporting growth in the Elk Grove Technology Park and the wider Western O'Hare real estate market, citing a Cushman and Wakefield ranking of the Chicago region as second globally for data center growth opportunity, though ComEd's own announcement names the broader technology sector generally rather than Equinix specifically as the driver of that investment. No Cook County assessor record, Elk Grove Village building permit, or contested zoning hearing specific to 1905 Lunt Avenue was located and confirmed in this research.

sources.title: ComEd Completes New Elk Grove Substation to Support Continued Growth of Illinois' Technology Sector
How One Village Became Home to North America's Largest Industrial Park

reading.body:
Equinix CH3 sits at 1905 Lunt Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, a Chicago suburb adjacent to O'Hare International Airport within what the Daily Herald describes as North America's largest industrial park. Equinix opened the facility in phases beginning October 2007 after a 175 million dollar conversion of an office and warehouse complex, absorbing over 300 customers from two smaller Chicago area locations. The building currently discloses 196,151 square feet of colocation space, though contractor accounts from different phases describe larger footprints of 228,000, 240,000, and 379,662 square feet, reflecting shell or total building measurements at different points in the site's expansion over nearly two decades.

Equinix publishes no current megawatt capacity figure for CH3. A contractor account from a later expansion phase states 10.8 megawatts at N+1 power redundancy for a larger building footprint, but this is not Equinix's published claim for the current facility. The facility meets Equinix's stated specifications of N+1 UPS redundancy, two generators with over 30 hours of autonomy at full load, and N+20 percent cooling redundancy. If the 10.8 megawatt figure applied to current operations, a common AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack would suggest roughly 270 racks of IT load, though this remains a contractor's historical account, not a current operator specification.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and 236 published megawatts of capacity across six operator-disclosed sites. CH3 ranks seventh in the state by published megawatt capacity, though Equinix does not publish its megawatt figure for this building individually. ComEd completed a new five acre substation in Elk Grove in November 2021 to expand regional transmission capacity supporting data center growth generally in the Western O'Hare technology market, per ComEd's announcement, without naming specific tenants or operators.
